ClaudeWatch.pitch: Screens every command before it runs — blocks the genuinely dangerous, asks before the rest, and stops you rubber-stamping the safe ones.
ClaudeWatch.what: Screens every shell command — and the code Claude writes to disk — before it runs, matching real patterns rather than naive prefixes, so reordered flags and chained commands don't slip past. Blocks the genuinely dangerous; asks before anything that changes state.

anchor.gloss: An anchor holds a boat in place. This holds your work in place.
anchor.pitch: Nervous about keeping code you didn't write? It walks you through the diff first, then commits with a why-first message and opens the change request.
anchor.what: Keeps your commits, change requests, and review cycles consistent — the same quality, formatting, and content every time. It walks you through the diff, then commits with a why-first message and opens the change request.

moor.gloss: To moor is to tie up alongside and look the hull over.
moor.pitch: A tighter review loop — step through the AI's changes and send each rejection straight back to Claude.
moor.what: A fast diff viewer for reading code the AI wrote — step through it one change at a time, accept or reject each with a note. anchor opens whatever diff viewer git is set to use; moor is a quick one built for this, and it feeds your notes back to Claude in context.

setup.head: Use as your git diff tool
setup.note: moor isn't wired in by claude plugin install, and there's no CLI flag for it — it's a one-time git setting. just git-install builds the app and points git at moor: it sets diff.tool to moor and difftool.moor.cmd to moor's launcher. After that, git difftool — and anchor — open moor for review.

tack.gloss: To tack is to change course; tack remembers every course you've held.
tack.pitch: Keep losing your place between sessions? It remembers what you were doing so you don't re-explain it every time.
tack.what: Tracks what you're working on — across crashes, context overflow, or jumping between projects. Start a fresh session and pick up exactly where you left off, instead of re-explaining everything.

beacon.gloss: A lighthouse you can read from across the harbor.
beacon.pitch: Running several Claude windows? Each gets a badge showing whether it's working or waiting on you.
beacon.what: Puts a colored badge on each terminal window so you can tell what every Claude session is doing at a glance: green idle, amber working, red waiting on you. Look away and still know which window needs you.

sextant.gloss: Fixes your position against a fixed reference — your spec.
sextant.pitch: Keeps requirements in source control, synced with the code either direction — so the spec, not the chat, is the source of truth.
sextant.what: Keeps a plain-language spec — what the code must do — under source control, and reconciles it with the code in either direction. The spec stays the durable source of truth — enough to rebuild an implementation from, not just describe one.

logbook.gloss: The ship's log — what the last crew figured out.
logbook.pitch: Solved something the hard way? It writes up what you learned and shares it with the team, so no one re-solves it.
logbook.what: Turns a session into a retrospective committed to a team-owned repo. Your chat transcript stays on your machine — only the write-up is shared, so the next person inherits the lesson, not just the code.
